title: Career roadmap · SOC Analyst
summary: Build practical skills in network security, Linux, threat detection, SIEM, incident response, digital forensics, scripting, and security operations to enter a Security Operations Centre and progress into incident-response and threat-hunting roles.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a standard 3-year BCA. A 4-year honours route can use the additional year for advanced SOC operations, threat hunting, malware analysis, cloud security, security research, and an industry internship.

about.label: Course alignment
about.text: SOC Analyst is directly aligned with BCA - Cyber Security / Ethical Hacking.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build networking, Linux, security fundamentals, SIEM, log analysis and incident-response skills; target SOC Intern / Security Analyst Intern / Junior SOC Analyst roles.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Develop expertise in threat detection, SIEM engineering, incident response, threat intelligence, endpoint security and cloud security.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress toward Senior SOC Analyst, Incident Responder, Threat Hunter, Detection Engineer or Security Engineer.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine security operations with cloud security, AI-assisted detection, automation, identity security, threat intelligence and security engineering.

blocks.text: Use Year 4 for advanced threat hunting, malware analysis, cloud security, detection engineering, digital forensics, security automation and security research. A strong final project could be a home SOC using a SIEM, endpoint telemetry and a documented incident-response workflow.

blocks.text: SOC work is becoming increasingly automated. Learn to supervise and improve automated detection rather than competing with automation. Build expertise in detection engineering, cloud telemetry, identity attacks, threat hunting, security automation, AI-assisted triage and adversary behaviour.

blocks.text: Progression varies by organisation and security specialisation.
A PhD is primarily useful for security research, academia, advanced threat research or specialised R&D rather than ordinary SOC operations.

SOC work will increasingly use AI for alert correlation, enrichment and triage. The durable skill is therefore not simply “knowing a SIEM.” Build expertise in detection engineering, threat hunting, identity security, cloud telemetry, adversary behaviour, automation and AI-assisted security operations.
